Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes use a\\nconsistent IOPS rate, which you specify when you create the volume. Amazon EBS delivers the\\nprovisioned performance 99.9 percent of the time.\\n\\n* `io1` volumes are designed to provide 99.8 to 99.9 percent volume durability\\n with an annual failure rate (AFR) no higher than 0.2 percent, which translates to a\\n maximum of two volume failures per 1,000 running volumes over a one-year period.\\n* `io2` and `io2` Block Express volumes are designed to provide\\n 99.999 percent volume durability with an AFR no higher than 0.001 percent, which\\n translates to a single volume failure per 100,000 running volumes over a one-year period.\\n\\nProvisioned IOPS SSD `io1` and `io2` volumes are available for all\\nAmazon EC2 instance types. Provisioned IOPS SSD `io2` volumes attached to\\n`c6in`, `c7g`, `m6in`, `m6idn`,\\n`r5b`, `r6in`, `r6idn`, `trn1`,\\n`x2idn`, and `x2iedn` instances run on Amazon EBS Block Express.\\n\\nProvisioned IOPS SSD volumes can range in size from 4 GiB to 16 TiB, and you can provision\\nfrom 100 IOPS up to 64,000 IOPS per volume. You can achieve up to 64,000 IOPS only on Instances built on the Nitro System. This provides dedicated throughput between\\nAmazon EBS volume and Amazon EC2 instance. On other instance families you can achieve performance up to\\n32,000 IOPS. The maximum ratio of provisioned IOPS to requested volume size (in GiB) is 50:1\\nfor `io1` volumes, and 500:1 for `io2` volumes.\\n\\n`io2` Block Express volumes are the next generation of Amazon EBS storage server\\narchitecture. Range is 100 to 64,000 IOPS for volumes in most\\nRegions. Maximum IOPS of 64,000 is guaranteed only on Nitro-based\\ninstances. Other instance families guarantee performance up to\\n32,000 IOPS. For more information, see Amazon EBS volume types in\\nthe *Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide*.\\n\\nThis parameter is valid only for Provisioned IOPS SSD (`io1` and `io2`)\\nvolumes.\\n\\nReturns:\\n\\n* (Integer)\\n \u2014\\n\\n The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for an `io1` or `io2` volume, with a maximum ratio of 50 IOPS/GiB for `io1`, and 500 IOPS/GiB for `io2`\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-ruby/v2/api/Aws/EC2/Types/CreateVolumeRequest.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up EBS io2 IOPS quota documentation"}

{"id": "9242d9ca-5475-43ad-b379-27b8c856ae66", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You've hit the account's regional quota for total provisioned io2 IOPS. This isn't a limit on a single volume. The 150K request is fine for a volume, because io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume. The error means your account can only have 100,000 io2 IOPS provisioned in total in that region, across all io2 volumes. Existing io2 volumes count toward that total, so your new volume has to fit in whatever is left.

**What to do**

1. **Request a quota increase (the usual fix).**
   - Open Service Quotas, go to Amazon EBS, and find **"IOPS for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes"**.
   - Request a value that covers your existing io2 IOPS plus the 150K. Make sure you're in the same region where the create failed.
   - You can also do this with the CLI: `aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ebs --quota-code <code> --desired-value <value> --region <region>`. Look up the quota code with `aws service-quotas list-service-quotas --service-code ebs`.
   - Small increases are often approved automatically. Large ones may go to AWS Support for review.

2. **Check how much of the quota you're already using.** Run `aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=volume-type,Values=io2` and add up the IOPS values. If old or unused io2 volumes are using up the quota, you may be able to free room by lowering their IOPS or removing them. Check that nothing depends on them first.

3. **Check that the workload can use the IOPS.** Per-volume IOPS above 64,000 only applies to io2 Block Express volumes attached to Nitro-based instances. On other instance types you're limited to about 32,000 IOPS. Also keep the ratio of IOPS to size in mind. io2 Block Express allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB, so 150K IOPS needs a volume of at least 150 GiB.

4. **If you need the volume right now,** create it with fewer IOPS (up to the quota you have left). Once the increase is approved, raise the IOPS with `modify-volume`. You can do this while the volume is in use.

If you tell me the region and account, I can look up your current io2 quota and add up the IOPS on your existing io2 volumes. That would show how much of the increase you need.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
